sourceEdition: 2021 Illustrative Mathematics K–5 source teacher lesson and Student Facing
sourceActivity1: Students draw one-third then one-quarter of that third AND one-quarter then one-third of that quarter as two diagrams; each shaded area is 1/12 of the original whole.
sourceActivity2: Interpret Priya's published 1/5×1/2 and 1/2×1/5 expressions as 1/10 of the original square; then write and justify a matching multiplication expression for the different source-provided shaded image, whose shading must not be guessed from a text-only replacement.
studentFacingFormativeTask: Draw two equal-size full-unit squares. Shade one fourth of one third in the first and one third of one fourth in the second. Compare their shaded areas and explain why both are 1/12 of the ORIGINAL whole. Then explain a separate 1/5×1/2 square and write both 1/5×1/2 and 1/2×1/5 for the same one-tenth area.

rubric.criterion: Both complete equal-size original unit squares are shown and explicitly identified as wholes
First square is partitioned into three equal thirds and one chosen third into four equal parts; full-square equal-area coverage
Second square partitions into four equal quarters and one selected quarter into three equal parts; full-square equal-area coverage
One marked cell of twelve, same absolute area in both orders; 1/12 of original whole justified
Priya example explains both 1/5×1/2 and 1/2×1/5 as 1/10 of the same whole, not 1/5 or 1/2 of whole
Source-provided separate shaded diagram receives its own correctly matched multiplication expression with a visual justification, not an assumed answer

rejectOrReview: shaded 1/3 or 1/4 of whole rather than 1/12
numeric-only exact answer without a diagram is insufficient for teacher construction criteria
incorrect expression for second original shaded diagram
